name: Carotid Web
aliases: Intimal Fibroplasia of the Carotid Artery

criteria.description: Identification of a shelf-like intimal projection in the carotid bulb on imaging (CTA, MRA, or DSA)
History of cryptogenic ischemic stroke or transient ischemic attack in the ipsilateral cerebral hemisphere
Absence of significant atherosclerotic disease or other vascular abnormalities explaining symptoms
Histopathological confirmation of intimal fibrous proliferation if surgical specimen available

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of imaging evidence of carotid web plus history of ipsilateral cryptogenic ischemic stroke or TIA, with exclusion of other vascular causes
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Diagnosis relies heavily on high-resolution vascular imaging and clinical correlation.

pathognomonic.notes: Stroke without identifiable cause other than carotid web
searchTerms: repeated unexplained strokes on one side
multiple strokes in same brain hemisphere

pathognomonic.symptomName: Transient ischemic attack localized to carotid territory
searchTerms: brief stroke-like symptoms in carotid area
temporary blood flow blockage in carotid territory
short-lasting ischemic attacks near carotid artery

common.symptomName: Focal neurological deficits consistent with middle cerebral artery ischemia
searchTerms: localized neurological deficits from MCA stroke
focal brain deficits due to MCA ischemia
loss of part of the vision field
blind spots or missing areas in vision

occasional.symptomName: Headache localized to ipsilateral carotid region
searchTerms: headache on same side as carotid artery
pain localized to carotid region of head
pain or tenderness in neck area
brief loss of vision in single eye

rare.notes: Due to carotid artery involvement affecting sympathetic chain

imaging: Computed tomography angiography (CTA) showing shelf-like intimal projection at carotid bulb
Magnetic resonance angiography (MRA) demonstrating focal web-like filling defect
Digital subtraction angiography (DSA) confirming characteristic web morphology
genetic: Possible familial clustering reported but not confirmed
other: Histopathology reveals intimal fibrous proliferation without atherosclerosis
Hemodynamic studies may show turbulent flow distal to web

distinguishingFeatures: Presence of lipid-rich plaques with calcifications
Risk factors such as hyperlipidemia and smoking
Intimal flap with double lumen on imaging
Acute neck pain and Horner syndrome more common
History of trauma or connective tissue disorder
Beaded appearance of arterial wall on angiography

redFlags: Recurrent cryptogenic strokes despite antiplatelet therapy
Transient monocular blindness or amaurosis fugax
references: Choi PM, Singh D, Trivedi A, et al. Carotid web and ischemic stroke: A systematic review and meta-analysis. Stroke. 2020;51(7):e133-e137.
Nouh A, Remke J, Ruland S. Carotid Web: An Unusual Cause of Ischemic Stroke. J Stroke Cerebrovasc Dis. 2016;25(7):e51-e54.
Satti SR, Suri MF, Mandell DM, et al. Carotid Web: An Underrecognized Cause of Cryptogenic Stroke. AJNR Am J Neuroradiol. 2015;36(11):2134-2139.
